Let \(l:y=0\) and \(m:y=2r\), so \(C_1\) has center \((0,r)\) and radius \(r\).

Since \(C_2\) is tangent to \(l\) and \(C_1\), its center is \((\pm 6\sqrt{r},9)\), because
\[
\sqrt{(6\sqrt r)^2+(9-r)^2}=r+9.
\]
Since \(C_3\) is tangent to \(m\) and \(C_1\) on the same side of \(m\), its center is \((\pm 4\sqrt{r},2r-4)\), because
\[
\sqrt{(4\sqrt r)^2+(r-4)^2}=r+4.
\]
Choose the same horizontal sign so the horizontal separation is \(2\sqrt r\). The distance between \(C_2\) and \(C_3\) must be \(9+4=13\):
\[
(2\sqrt r)^2+(2r-13)^2=13^2.
\]
Thus
\[
4r+(2r-13)^2=169
\]
\[
4r+4r^2-52r+169=169
\]
\[
4r^2-48r=0
\]
\[
4r(r-12)=0.
\]
Since \(r>0\), \(r=12\).

\[
\boxed{12}
\]
